subject: Human Body
title: Bile and Fat Digestion
description: One-minute skill: Bile and Fat Digestion.

hook.text: Oil and water don't mix. That's a problem because your enzymes are water-based and fats are oily.

buildup.text: Bile is a yellowish-green fluid made by the liver and stored in the gallbladder until needed.

discovery.text: Bile acts like dish soap. It breaks fat globules into tiny droplets — a process called emulsification.

twist.text: Without bile, you absorb less than half the fat you eat. Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K are lost too.

climax.text: Bile doesn't digest fat directly. It prepares fat for lipase, the enzyme that actually breaks fat apart.

punchline.text: Bile is the soap. Lipase is the scrubber. Both are needed.

quiz.question: What does bile do to fat?
options: Absorbs it directly into the blood
Breaks it into small droplets for enzyme access
